DovunOxlY1k.summary: A Bell Labs film in which Dr. J.N. Shive uses a mechanical wave machine to demonstrate reflection, standing waves, resonance and impedance matching. He includes some equations but relies mostly on real-world examples a layperson can follow.
DovunOxlY1k.why: HN repeatedly calls it the clearest introduction to waves and transmission-line behavior, better than modern explainers.

D1R-jKKp3NA.summary: Steve Jobs's 2005 Stanford commencement address, built around three stories: connecting the dots, love and loss including being fired from Apple, and death. It is a 15-minute talk on finding work you love.
D1R-jKKp3NA.why: HN returns to it for years as an inspirational talk to send to graduates, founders and anyone at a career crossroads.

DnPmg0R1M04.summary: The first part of Adam Curtis' documentary series on Sigmund Freud and his nephew Edward Bernays, who invented public relations. It shows how Bernays used Freud's ideas to link mass-produced goods to unconscious desires and create modern consumer persuasion.
DnPmg0R1M04.why: HN commenters recommend it constantly in threads about advertising, propaganda and manipulation as the origin story of the consumer society.

D6h5dFyyUX0.summary: A three-minute Emacs Rocks screencast by Magnar Sveen demonstrating paredit, which edits Lisp code structurally as a tree of s-expressions rather than characters.
D6h5dFyyUX0.why: Repeatedly offered as the quickest, most convincing demo of structured editing and why Lisp programmers love paredit.

DkS1pkKpILY.summary: A two-hour Huberman Lab podcast episode on the physiological effects of alcohol on the brain and body at different levels of consumption. It covers genetic predisposition to alcoholism, alcohol metabolism, and how it causes cellular stress and changes thinking and behavior.
DkS1pkKpILY.why: HN commenters say it convinced them to quit or cut down on drinking, and point to it as a more comprehensive treatment than most articles.

Dp-mQ3HxgDE.summary: Mathematician Kevin Buzzard explains why he believes the Lean theorem prover will shape the future of mathematics, and describes digitizing his university curriculum in Lean with undergraduates, plus the cultural challenges.
Dp-mQ3HxgDE.why: Recommended as the clearest mathematician's perspective on formal proof assistants and why mathematics should be formalized.

D99qI42KGB0.summary: Potholer54 presents the climate science case and a market-oriented, conservative-friendly approach to addressing global warming, with sources listed. It is part one of a two-part series.
D99qI42KGB0.why: HN users recommend it as a model of communicating climate science to conservative and libertarian audiences without alienating them.

D9H9qTdserM.summary: Robert Sapolsky's lecture on how the body's stress response, evolved for short-term physical emergencies, harms long-term health when triggered by psychological stressors. It was given as the inaugural Fenton-Rhodes Lecture.
D9H9qTdserM.why: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining and informative explanation of how stress affects health.

DJtef410XaM.summary: Brandon Rhodes' PyOhio 2014 talk on applying the Clean Architecture in Python. He shows how this high-level design pattern fits Python's features and addresses maintainability problems in large applications.
DJtef410XaM.why: HN points to it as a practical way to separate business logic from I/O, which reduces mocking and underlies the functional core, imperative shell idea.

DZCBRHOg3PQ.summary: A three-hour-plus Joe Rogan podcast with Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey, policy lead Vijaya Gadde and journalist Tim Pool. They discuss Twitter's moderation, bans and rule enforcement, with Pool challenging Dorsey and Gadde with examples.
DZCBRHOg3PQ.why: HN people cite it as insight into how Twitter thought about moderation, and as a source for Tim Pool's arguments about uneven enforcement.

DleXA5ADG78.summary: Geoffrey Hinton's Google Tech Talk linking machine learning to biology, explaining dropout as a form of model averaging and why sexual reproduction and stochastic spiking neurons may prevent overfitting.
DleXA5ADG78.why: Recommended as a simple, elegant explanation of dropout and its connection to how the brain works.

DpXy041BIlA.summary: Tom Scott-style absurdist tour by Tom7 of SIGBOVIK chess projects: a tournament of 30 weird chess algorithms used to rate a color- and piece-blind chess program. Topics include mirrors, arithmetic encoding, perverted game tree search and a diluted Stockfish.
DpXy041BIlA.why: HN commenters call it a must-watch for its deadpan, absurdly elaborate engineering and cite it for ideas like diluting strong engines with random moves.

DgVS-zXgMTk.summary: Pete Hunt of Facebook and Instagram presents React at JSConf.Asia 2013, explaining its design principles and why they seemed shocking at first. He argues that React separates concerns rather than technologies, and the talk also announces the React Chrome developer tools.
DgVS-zXgMTk.why: HN commenters credit it with persuading them to adopt React, and cite it for the argument that HTML and JS cannot truly be separated.

DmT80OseAGs.summary: A Dyalog demonstration of developing a Sudoku solver in APL, using an algorithm by Arthur Whitney with performance work by John Scholes. The narration steps through the array-oriented solution.
DmT80OseAGs.why: Strongly recommended as a beautiful demonstration that APL can be read and reasoned about step by step.

DkGMY63FF3Q.summary: An Onion Talks satire in which a young media professional pitches compost-powered cars, offering the idea itself and leaving all implementation to others.
DkGMY63FF3Q.why: HN uses it as shorthand for vague, detail-free visionary pitches and as a satirical jab at TED-style techno-utopian talks.

DOWDNBu9DkU.summary: Mark Rober visits Zipline and looks at its autonomous delivery drones, including medical and blood deliveries in Rwanda. He demonstrates how the drones' propeller design and cable-lowered delivery pod make them quiet and precise.
DOWDNBu9DkU.why: HN commenters cite it as the clearest look at Zipline's real-world drone operations, especially for medical delivery and the solved noise problem.

DEcwa68f-jY.summary: James Long's dotJS 2019 talk on how CRDTs enable local-first apps and how simple they can be to implement. He shows how to use them to build robust offline-capable frontends.
DEcwa68f-jY.why: Recommended as an approachable introduction to CRDTs and the local-first idea behind apps like Actual.

DRq2NgeFcO0.summary: Edwin Brady, creator of Idris, presents Idris 2 and demonstrates type-driven development, where the compiler assists by filling holes and suggesting implementations from types.
DRq2NgeFcO0.why: Recommended as the best demo of interactive, compiler-assisted dependently typed programming in action.

Dddbe9OuJLU.summary: The first episode of Jason Scott's eight-part BBS documentary, covering the predecessors and beginnings of the dial-up bulletin board system. It includes interviews with pioneers such as Ward Christensen and Randy Suess, who created the first dial-up BBS in 1978.
Dddbe9OuJLU.why: HN commenters recommend the series as the definitive history of BBS culture and its Fidonet roots, especially for nostalgia and the origins of the demoscene.

DsZdfnlh_d0.summary: John Scholes builds a depth-first tree-search operator step by step in a Dyalog APL session. It covers higher-order functions and runs the search on the N-Queens problem.
DsZdfnlh_d0.why: HN commenters call it a beautiful, brilliant demonstration of APL's expressiveness and a model of clear narration.

DxL2HoqLbyA.summary: Veritasium's explainer on entropy, presented as one of physics' most important and least understood concepts. It uses examples such as heat engines and the sun's energy flowing through the Earth.
DxL2HoqLbyA.why: HN commenters say it made entropy intuition click and point to it in threads on energy, heat and equilibrium.

D6EPuUdIC1E.summary: A cardiologist runs a detailed, skeptical review of the Wim Hof Method, covering the research on cold exposure and breathing techniques. It also teaches how to read scientific statistics critically.
D6EPuUdIC1E.why: HN points people to it as a nuanced, medically informed take whenever Wim Hof breathing or cold plunges come up.

DFFVSvAr7Wc.summary: Physicist Geoffrey West speaks at an FQXi conference on time about complexity and scaling laws. He covers how metabolism, growth and lifespan scale across organisms and how the same mathematics applies to cities and companies.
DFFVSvAr7Wc.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible introduction to scaling laws and to why cities keep growing while companies and organisms eventually die.

DShDaJXK5qo.summary: An episode of Gwynne Dyer's 1983 documentary series War, about how military basic training turns recruits into soldiers. It covers the psychological side of conditioning.
DShDaJXK5qo.why: Recommended as a classic documentary on military training and the psychology of going to war.

DXvAlwMAxiA.summary: Ben Eater gives a detailed look at how an NPN bipolar junction transistor works and what it does. It is an eleven-minute explanation aimed at building real understanding of the device.
DXvAlwMAxiA.why: HN commenters prefer it over other transistor explanations as an enlightening starting point that leads into building logic gates and a CPU.

DoeNbZlxfUM.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's DEF CON 18 talk argues that privacy threats have shifted from centralized state databases like TIA to corporate data collection by companies like Google, despite wins in strong cryptography and decentralization.
DoeNbZlxfUM.why: Strongly recommended as a formative talk on privacy, especially for its argument that voting with your feet fails as a privacy strategy.

D5xh0ZIEUOE.summary: James Mickens delivers his comedic rant about JavaScript and web programming, in his usual dry, hyperbolic style. It includes his account of learning the language from the O'Reilly Definitive Guide.
D5xh0ZIEUOE.why: HN recommends it as a hilarious talk by a beloved speaker, and also uses it to jab at JavaScript's quirks.

D7Sd8A6_fYU.summary: Dan Saks's CppCon 2016 talk on why C programmers resist C++ and how to talk to them about it. He argues that persuasion rarely works by arguing and examines the culture gap between the two communities.
D7Sd8A6_fYU.why: Recommended in C versus C++ and embedded threads as the expert view on adoption and persuasion.

DC8tO16xdrY.summary: The first part of a long two-part video series by historian Sean Munger arguing, with citations, that Lee Harvey Oswald assassinated President Kennedy and acted alone. It goes through the provable historical facts and addresses conspiracy theories.
DC8tO16xdrY.why: HN commenters recommend it as the most exhaustive, well-sourced rebuttal of JFK conspiracy theories, often when new assassination claims surface.

DJFKl_5JTnA.summary: Turing Award winner Michael Stonebraker gives the 2018 Donald B. Gillies Memorial Lecture at Illinois. He discusses the gap between academic research and industry problems, publishing incentives, and the influence of large industry users on research.
DJFKl_5JTnA.why: Cited in many threads about academic incentives, paper counts and why academia struggles to produce working software.

DkMwYxfSYNQ.summary: Jon Gjengset's long live-coding stream explains Rust's Pin and Unpin types: why they exist, how they work, and how they connect to futures and async/await. It also covers moving from pre-pinning code to the new model.
DkMwYxfSYNQ.why: HN treats it as the definitive resource for understanding Pin semantics and lists it among async Rust learning materials.

DYvhC_RdIwQ.summary: A short KRAZAM comedy sketch satirizing corporate tech life, where a worker reckons with having delivered value at the cost of his soul, complete with Slack chimes.
DYvhC_RdIwQ.why: Praised as painfully accurate office satire, with the channel's sketches called genius.

DlTq8DbRs4k.summary: Wendover Productions explains how UK rail privatization worked and why it failed. It covers the fragmented operator and infrastructure structure and why market forces apply poorly to rail.
DlTq8DbRs4k.why: Recommended in privatization and rail threads as a clear, well-sourced explanation of the UK rail mess.

DlkMs4ZHHr8.summary: A bot built by Robin Baumgarten plays Infinite Mario using A* path-finding, shown as a red planned path that updates as new obstacles appear. It won the Mario AI competitions and uses only on-screen information.
DlkMs4ZHHr8.why: HN points to it as a vivid demo that plain A* search can beat fancier machine-learning approaches in game AI.

DwKPFT-RioU.summary: Neil Halloran's animated, data-driven documentary visualizes the human cost of World War II and compares it with other wars and the trend toward fewer war deaths in recent decades.
DwKPFT-RioU.why: HN cites it for a sense of the scale of WWII casualties by country and the long decline in violence.

D5in5EdjhD0.summary: Noam Chomsky's 2011 University of Oslo lecture on Newton's contributions to the study of mind. He argues Newton abandoned mechanical explanation and lowered the bar for scientific intelligibility, with consequences for the limits of human understanding. Q&A starts at 45:33.
D5in5EdjhD0.why: Recommended as a lucid, insightful lecture on the limits of human knowledge and the study of mind, one commenter calling it among the best lectures ever.

D7Kn5p7TP_Y.summary: A Jordan Peterson university lecture on the Big Five trait openness to experience, covering creativity and intelligence. It explains how IQ is measured, how well it predicts life success, and the Pareto distribution of creative output.
D7Kn5p7TP_Y.why: Recommended as a solid introduction to personality and IQ research, and cited as the source for factor-analysis claims about personality and intelligence.

DBxdTkddHaE.summary: Tod's Workshop fires full-weight medieval arrows from a 160lb English warbow at reproduced medieval armour. Armour curator Dr Tobias Capwell, an archer and bowyer give historical context and discuss the results.
DBxdTkddHaE.why: HN considers it the key experimental evidence on how effective longbows really were against armour.

DQEB3LJ5psk.summary: Part one of Sandia National Labs' first-person documentary on the use control, detonation safety and survivability of US nuclear weapons. It covers nuclear sharing in NATO and how control of use was separated from possession, leading to the always/never problem.
DQEB3LJ5psk.why: Strongly recommended in nuclear-accident and weapons-history threads as an excellent documentary on how nuclear weapons were made safe and secure.

DXYje2B04xE.summary: Shahriar of The Signal Path tears down and experiments with Keysight's UXR real-time oscilloscope, which offers 110GHz bandwidth and 256GS/s sampling, and compares architectures from Keysight, LeCroy and Tektronix.
DXYje2B04xE.why: Recommended as part of a channel with deep teardowns of extreme test equipment, valuable for anyone interested in electronics or RF.

DCto6UkBJoI.summary: Scott Manley examines why SpaceX, Google and others are looking at orbital data centers. He walks through the economics, heat rejection and solar power arguments, with links to the Lumen/Starcloud and Google Suncatcher papers.
DCto6UkBJoI.why: Pointed to as a credible, engineering-informed answer to whether space data centers are feasible, from someone with deep space knowledge.

DKtVpvzUF1Y.summary: Raw 500 fps footage from Camera E-8 on the launch tower for the Apollo 11 Saturn V liftoff, transferred in HD from the 16mm original. More than eight minutes of film covers about 30 seconds of real time.
DKtVpvzUF1Y.why: HN commenters recommend it for its slow-motion view of the first seconds of liftoff and cite it when comparing launch pads and engine behavior.

DSjbTC-hvqQ.summary: Evan Czaplicki, creator of Elm, gives an elm-conf 2016 talk on the non-code side of building a language. It covers the philosophy behind Elm's development approach, including batching work and the priorities of different language communities.
DSjbTC-hvqQ.why: HN points people to it to understand Elm's design philosophy, such as favoring simplicity over type classes, when they question its choices.

DUGGJpn2_zY.summary: The fail0verflow team (bushing, marcan, sven) present console hacking at 27C3, covering Wii, Xbox 360 and PS3 exploits. They explain how the PS3 was cracked after Sony removed Other OS.
DUGGJpn2_zY.why: HN recommends it as the primary source on Sony's ECDSA nonce-reuse blunder and the history of console cracking.

DZTIbHIsIYw.summary: A social experiment in which an 18-year-old woman runs a Tinder profile as a man and sees how differently the dating experience plays out for men.
DZTIbHIsIYw.why: HN brings it up in dating app threads as a real-world illustration of how hard Tinder is for men.

Dar8P3r7GYA.summary: A TED conversation with SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell about the company's race to put people in orbit and the BFR rocket. It also covers the idea of using the rocket for fast point-to-point travel on Earth.
Dar8P3r7GYA.why: Pointed to in SpaceX threads as a window into the company's ambitions and leadership.

DdM-XTRyC9c.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's 36C3 talk examines why distributed and decentralized technology is hard to build into consumer products, from the perspective of developing Signal. It argues that ecosystems move slowly and federation causes problems.
DdM-XTRyC9c.why: Cited in decentralization and federation debates as the key talk on the practical challenges, though some found it defeatist.

DoA4Txr4GUs.summary: Richard Feldman's Elm Europe 2017 talk on how to structure and scale large Elm applications, including when to nest messages.
DoA4Txr4GUs.why: The standard pointer for anyone asking how to organize larger Elm codebases.

D28uSzCs7-k.summary: Marco Reps builds and tests an open-source 8.5 digit voltmeter based on CERN's high-precision ADC design. The video walks through assembly, soldering and measurement of the resulting instrument.
D28uSzCs7-k.why: HN people point to it as a showcase of CERN's open hardware and as an example of quality metrology content.

Dw3BZ6O_8LY.summary: Yosh trains a reinforcement learning agent to drive Trackmania until he can no longer beat it. The video explains how the training works and the design choices involved.
Dw3BZ6O_8LY.why: Recommended as an approachable explanation of how reinforcement learning works in practice, and cited for the constraints needed to stop exploits.

Dxnr2FAADAs.summary: Valve opens up a Steam Deck to show its internal components and explain which are replaceable or upgradable. It advises against self-repair but shares the details openly.
Dxnr2FAADAs.why: HN praises its openness and respect for the customer, and cites it as a precedent for manufacturers showing internals.

D2vj0WcvH5c.summary: A short Tesla clip showing the Optimus humanoid robot sorting objects autonomously and doing yoga-style stretches. Tesla says its neural network is trained end to end, from video in to controls out.
D2vj0WcvH5c.why: Linked as a data point on the state of humanoid robot manipulation in 2023.

D38dcArwCNc.summary: A follow-up review of using e-ink devices, such as Onyx Boox tablets, for productivity and as a second monitor. It covers software tips and tweaks and long-term impressions after months of use.
D38dcArwCNc.why: Cited in e-ink display threads as a long-term review of using e-ink as a monitor.

D7GDTZ45TRw.summary: A long Mill Computing lecture on the Mill CPU's compiler toolchain, covering the specializer that targets family members, scheduling and latency passes, and the belt. It explains how the compiler handles a wide-issue, exposed-pipeline design.
D7GDTZ45TRw.why: Cited as the authoritative source on how Mill's VLIW-style compiler specializes code and differs from Itanium.

DEEr6dT-4uQ.summary: Kirk McKusick gives a narrative history of the Berkeley Software Distributions at MeetBSD California. He covers how BSD originated and evolved, including the origin of the networking releases.
DEEr6dT-4uQ.why: Recommended as the authoritative, first-hand telling of BSD lore whenever Unix and BSD history comes up.

DGscoaUWW2M.summary: A short clip from the BBC sitcom Yes, Prime Minister in which Jim Hacker explains which kind of person reads which British newspaper. It is a satirical take on press readership and bias.
DGscoaUWW2M.why: Posted as a joke and a reference whenever threads discuss newspaper bias and media pandering to readers.

DOW_kPzY_JY.summary: A short scene from The Office US in which Michael Scott blindly follows his GPS and drives into a lake. The tagline is never trust technology.
DOW_kPzY_JY.why: HN people link it as a joke about blindly trusting navigation or automated systems.

DU8hg4FTm0g.summary: Chris Paget's DEF CON 18 talk on practical cellphone spying, showing how GSM traffic can be intercepted with a fake base station. It covers 2G interception and the weaknesses of cellular networks.
DU8hg4FTm0g.why: HN points to it as a worrying but technically solid explanation of how cell interception works, even if the talk is old.

DX73uXs3xGU.summary: InRangeTV's controlled mud test of an AKM, covering it in mud and testing whether it still fires, in a series that also tested the M1, M14 and AR-15.
DX73uXs3xGU.why: Used in AK versus AR reliability debates to show that the AK's legendary mud-proof reputation is overstated.

De0Am_QcZiQ.summary: Jonathan Blow's Reboot Develop 2017 talk on making game programming less terrible, discussing software bloat, slowness and the design goals behind his own programming language.
De0Am_QcZiQ.why: Cited in discussions of software getting slower and of efforts to reduce friction in programming.

DfznnKUwywQ.summary: A Disney Research SIGGRAPH 2013 demo of an interactive system that lets non-experts design animated mechanical characters. The user sketches motion curves and the system generates optimized mechanisms and gear trains for 3D printing.
DfznnKUwywQ.why: HN cites it as an example of computational mechanism design, especially in threads on gears, linkages and animatronics.

Dk306ZkNOuc.summary: A video tour of Apple's highly automated Macintosh factory in Fremont, California, where the Mac SE and Macintosh II were built.
Dk306ZkNOuc.why: Used as the visual reference for Apple's earlier US manufacturing and automation, often as an example of factory automation lessons.

DoQoeK53bP8.summary: A five-minute SuperMemo demo of incremental reading: importing a Wikipedia article on nutrition, extracting passages, making cloze deletions and finishing the item. It lists the keyboard shortcuts used.
DoQoeK53bP8.why: Pointed to as a short demonstration of what incremental reading looks like in practice, though one commenter was not convinced by it.

Ds-v2-qyCc8.summary: Not Just Bikes looks at the cancelled plan to spend over $200 million widening Wonderland Road, a stroad in his hometown of London, Ontario. He asks whether the cancellation marks a turning point away from car-dependent development.
Ds-v2-qyCc8.why: Mentioned in threads on stroads and road safety as an example of the channel's critique of wasteful car infrastructure.

DsVzKCk066g.summary: A video arguing that exercise matters for the brain as much as the body, linking movement, the nervous system and BDNF to learning and memory. It draws on research connecting complex movement to brain development.
DsVzKCk066g.why: Cited in threads on exercise and cognition as an accessible overview of the movement-brain connection.

DzRGBAUz5mA.summary: Linus Tech Tips addresses criticism of its clickbait-style thumbnails in an Honest Answers episode, explaining that the YouTube algorithm pushes creators toward them.
DzRGBAUz5mA.why: Referenced in clickbait and YouTube-algorithm debates as a candid creator explanation of why good channels use poor thumbnails.

D-On0DGcDlc.summary: LockPickingLawyer cuts through a LiteLok flexible bike lock with cable cutters in about 16 seconds, one of several videos defeating the product.
D-On0DGcDlc.why: Used in bike-lock discussions as evidence that the LiteLok is weak, and a reminder that LPL reviews are a trusted benchmark for lock security.

D1sXuHnf_lo.summary: A demo of Deldo, an Emacs package that lets Emacs hooks trigger vibration events on computer-controllable sex toys. It is an absurd teledildonics project that is half performance art.
D1sXuHnf_lo.why: HN mostly links it as a joke in Emacs threads, though one commenter calls the video the most interesting part of the Deldo project.

D2SoGHFM18I.summary: A short Discovery nature clip from North America showing a red fox listening for field mice under the snow and then diving headfirst to catch them. The narration says the fox uses its hearing and the Earth's magnetic field to aim its jump.
D2SoGHFM18I.why: HN commenters cite the footage as anecdotal evidence in threads about animals sensing the Earth's magnetic field, and for the head-tilt listening behavior.

D2fYguIX17Q.summary: A short clip from Woody Allen's 1973 film Sleeper in which a man who wakes up in the future is told that health foods are unhealthy and tobacco is good for you.
D2fYguIX17Q.why: HN posts it as a joke in threads about shifting nutrition and health science advice.

D4vHnM8WPvU.summary: A short animated excerpt of Alan Watts describing 'prickles' (rigorous, scientific types) and 'goo' (soft, spiritual types). He argues the real division is between prickly goo and gooey prickles.
D4vHnM8WPvU.why: HN uses it as shorthand for the divide between systematizing and humanistic outlooks, applied to arguments about science, society and language.

D5VN56jQMWM.summary: A short clip of the Google I/O 2018 demo in which Google Assistant's Duplex phones a salon and a restaurant to make appointments. The calls sound like a natural human conversation.
D5VN56jQMWM.why: Mostly cited as an example of an overhyped or possibly staged AI demo, alongside later skeptical comparisons to other company demos.

DAcjV60RnRw.summary: Vsauce asks whether music will ever run out of new melodies. It counts the possible note combinations and discusses how common chord progressions and remixing affect originality.
DAcjV60RnRw.why: HN uses it as the reference for counting how many songs or melodies are possible from a finite set of notes.

DEP8juRSBRo.summary: Stuntman Gary Connery jumps from a helicopter at 2,400 feet in a wingsuit and lands without a parachute on a runway of stacked cardboard boxes, the first such landing.
DEP8juRSBRo.why: Cited as an example of how padding can allow survival of very high-speed impacts.

DJklHwoYgBQ.summary: An Adult Swim infomercial parody for Smart Pipe, a fictional startup that turns toilet waste into data and social connectivity. It satirizes everything-connected tech culture.
DJklHwoYgBQ.why: HN posts it as a joke whenever a real smart toilet, IoT gadget or silly startup idea appears, because reality keeps matching the parody.

DNCZHAQnfGU.summary: A two-minute clip from a March 2005 House Budget Committee hearing in which Paul Ryan asks Alan Greenspan about personal retirement accounts and social security solvency. Greenspan replies that nothing prevents the government from creating as much money as it wants.
DNCZHAQnfGU.why: HN commenters use it as a primary-source clip for the argument that a currency-issuing government cannot go bankrupt in its own currency.

DPNK7bc2qvM.summary: Helmet-camera footage of linemen installing a spacer on an energized 765,000 volt transmission line, working from a helicopter. The crew bonds on and off the live wire as part of the job.
DPNK7bc2qvM.why: Cited as a striking example of live-line work and of potential equalization, with the air as the insulator.

DQ8orIurGxw.summary: carykh demonstrates a script that speeds up the silent parts of a video while leaving speech at normal speed, to condense lectures and similar footage. It later became the Jumpcutter tool.
DQ8orIurGxw.why: Referenced as the origin of automatic silence-skipping video editing and as a comparison for similar tools.

DWpBNm6lBU4.summary: A seven-minute Google I/O 2014 talk by Simon Newton on how developers can make use of Google's global network. It describes the network's footprint and some of the services running on it.
DWpBNm6lBU4.why: HN commenters, including a Googler, cite it as the public explanation of how Google serves traffic, including DNS-based load balancing.

DXUOWXidcY0.summary: A short demo of Automaton 2000 Micro, a StarCraft bot built in Blizzard's World Editor that splits marines perfectly against banelings. It shows inhuman unit micromanagement with zero losses.
DXUOWXidcY0.why: Cited in StarCraft AI threads to show how much perfect micro matters, though one commenter finds such play boring.

DbKNlFcg02c.summary: CGP Grey explains the history and legal status of territorial claims on Antarctica. It covers the overlapping national claims and the Antarctic Treaty that freezes them.
DbKNlFcg02c.why: Cited as a short explainer when Antarctic governance comes up, including as an analogy for governing Mars.

Dd7FixvoKBw.summary: A Key & Peele sketch in which an inner-city substitute teacher, Mr. Garvey, keeps mangling the names of his middle-class students during attendance.
Dd7FixvoKBw.why: HN commenters mention it as a joke in threads about names being mispronounced or causing problems.

DdmyUZCl75s.summary: A one-minute clip of Peter Norvig saying that Google found programming contest success correlates negatively or poorly with job performance. The description links to a blog post discussing it.
DdmyUZCl75s.why: Used as the go-to citation in LeetCode and hiring debates that competitive programming skill is not a good signal for hiring.

Dek5HtNdIHY.summary: A three-minute scene from season 2, episode 4 of Silicon Valley in which Jared is excited after the company hires a woman engineer. It satirizes tokenism in tech hiring.
Dek5HtNdIHY.why: HN commenters bring it up as a joke or shorthand in threads about diversity hiring and women in tech.

DgrO_rAaiq0.summary: The opening scene of The Wire season 5, in which detectives use a copy machine as a fake lie detector to get a confession.
DgrO_rAaiq0.why: Posted as a joke in polygraph and lie-detector threads.

Di3fPj0pUbQ.summary: A two-minute clip from Silicon Valley season 1, episode 7 featuring the human heater idea that is rejected in a startup competition scene.
Di3fPj0pUbQ.why: HN uses it mostly as a joke or to point out that the human heater idea comes from the sitcom.

DkUpZkeqhF4.summary: A 2013 lecture in which Vitalik Buterin explains what quantum computers are and what they can and cannot do. He then discusses what they could mean for Bitcoin's cryptography.
DkUpZkeqhF4.why: Mostly cited in critical or skeptical comments about Buterin, with a little admiration for the talk coming from a 19-year-old.

Dkw15LkZ_Kw.summary: A VICE News piece on China's Social Credit System, including a neighbor-watch pilot where paid watchers record behavior. It covers rewards for high scores and public shaming or restrictions for low ones.
Dkw15LkZ_Kw.why: Cited as a visual reference in discussions of social credit, surveillance and facial recognition in China, usually with a dystopian framing.

Dp4dpeJVDxs.summary: A clip from a BBC interview in which Richard Feynman is asked why magnets repel and attract. He explains that "why" questions depend on what a person already accepts as fundamental.
Dp4dpeJVDxs.why: Cited whenever a discussion turns to how hard it is to answer "why" questions or what counts as an explanation.
